claims.text: Chemical short-range order suppresses lattice thermal conductivity relative to a random solid solution in concentrated refractory high-entropy alloys.
Rapid solidification or high-temperature homogenization followed by quenching produces an SRO-suppressed random-solid-solution state.
For the proposed RHEAs, 800–1200 K is below the solvus but above the diffusion threshold for SRO formation.
Aging for 10–100 hours at 800–1200 K can produce equilibrium SRO, including L12- or L11-type clusters or diffuse ordering.
SRO domains create local variations in atomic mass and interatomic force constants.
SRO in MoNbTaW produces diffuse antiphase boundaries that impede dislocation motion and provide additional strengthening.
Diffuse antiphase boundaries associated with SRO scatter mid-to-long-wavelength phonons.
Random chemical disorder preferentially scatters short-wavelength phonons.
SRO domains in the relevant RHEAs have a characteristic size of approximately 1–2 nm.
SRO domains resonantly scatter phonons whose wavelengths are comparable to the domain size.
SRO adds a phonon-relaxation term distinct from random-alloy mass-difference scattering and thereby reduces the phonon mean free path.
Severe lattice distortion is a characteristic effect in concentrated high-entropy alloys.
Severe lattice distortion already suppresses lattice thermal conductivity in RHEAs to near-amorphous limits.
SRO aging will reduce lattice thermal conductivity by 10–25% relative to the quenched RSS state between 300 and 800 K.
The conductivity difference between SRO and RSS states will diminish above 1000 K because Umklapp scattering becomes dominant.
The SRO state will approach the theoretical minimum thermal conductivity more closely than the RSS state.
Random-solid-solution refractory alloys typically have thermal conductivities of 5–15 W m−1 K−1 because of severe lattice distortion and mass-variance scattering.
The proposed suppression applies to single-phase BCC or FCC refractory alloys in which SRO is thermodynamically stable.
SRO domains smaller than 0.5 nm will not effectively scatter the dominant phonon wavelengths.
If aging causes phase separation into precipitates, interface scattering rather than SRO-domain scattering becomes the relevant mechanism.
